verses.text: While Jehoiakim was king, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon invaded the land. Jehoiakim became his servant for three years, but then he turned and rebelled against him.
The LORD sent raiding parties of Babylonians, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites against Jehoiakim. He sent them to destroy Judah, just as the LORD had said through his servants the prophets.
These things happened to Judah because the LORD commanded it. He was removing them from his presence because of the sins of Manasseh and all he had done,
and also because of the innocent blood he had spilled. Manasseh had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD was not willing to forgive.
The rest of what Jehoiakim did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
Jehoiakim died, and his son Jehoiachin became king after him.
The king of Egypt did not march out of his country again, because the king of Babylon had taken all his land, from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for three months. His mother was Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan, from Jerusalem.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, just as his father had done.
At that time the officers of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked Jerusalem and surrounded the city.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon himself came to the city while his officers were surrounding it.

Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to surrender to the king of Babylon, along with his mother, his officials, his princes, and his officers. In the eighth year of his rule, the king of Babylon took Jehoiachin prisoner.

Nebuchadnezzar carried off all the treasures from the LORD's temple and from the palace. He cut into pieces all the gold objects Solomon king of Israel had made for the LORD's temple, just as the LORD had said would happen.

He took away all the people of Jerusalem as prisoners: all the princes and all the best soldiers, ten thousand people in all, along with all the skilled workers and metalworkers. Only the poorest people of the land were left.

Nebuchadnezzar took Jehoiachin away to Babylon. He also took the king's mother, the king's wives, his officials, and the leading men of the land. He took them all as prisoners from Jerusalem to Babylon.
The king of Babylon also took to Babylon all seven thousand of the fighting men and one thousand skilled workers and metalworkers. All of them were strong and ready for war.
The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, just as Jehoiakim had done.
It was because of the LORD's anger that all this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, until in the end he threw them out of his presence. Then Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
